fields.description: Identity of this record on the central AI Scan CRM site. One central record maps to exactly one Lead. NULL while the row is a placeholder written by the legacy field migration for a Lead that has a business but has never been pushed under protocol 1; the first push adopts the row and fills this in. UNIQUE ignores NULLs, so any number of placeholders can coexist -- but only one per Lead.
fields.label: Scan UUID

fields.description: JSON {"ids": [...], "dropped": N}: the request_ids this endpoint has already applied to this record, oldest first, most recent last, plus a count of the ones the window has forgotten. A re-delivery of any remembered id is answered without writing -- only the newest request has a stored response, and re-applying an older payload would silently revert the record. Past the window the write happens but the answer carries a warning saying it could not be checked. Rows written before this release hold a bare JSON array and are read as "nothing forgotten".
fields.label: Seen Request IDs

fields.description: Hash of the last accepted payload; an identical re-push is a no-op.
fields.label: Payload Hash

fields.description: Comma separated list of fields this connector wrote on the Lead.
fields.label: Migrated Fields

fields.description: JSON: the email addresses and phone numbers this client already held when the Lead was adopted and the central record had never sent. Re-merged on every later push, so an ordinary update cannot delete them; a value the client removes by hand drops out and is not resurrected.
fields.label: Client Held Contacts
